about: House recipes, batch 04 (helper sA): written by Claude in a Max-plan session, original, ai-draft. Nutrition is a per-serve estimate kept as data only.

recipes.title: Slow-Cooker Beef and Barley Stew with Root Vegetables
recipes.summary: A hearty stew of diced beef, pearl barley, carrot and potato that cooks all day while you are out.
steps: Brown the beef in the oil in batches for 5 minutes and tip into the slow cooker.
Add the onion, garlic, tomato paste, stock, bay leaves, carrot, potato and barley and stir well.
Cook on low for 8 hours until the beef is tender and the barley is soft, then remove the bay leaves and serve.
notes: Contains gluten.
Food safety: cook beef until tender and steaming hot throughout (at least 75°C); refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 3 days.

recipes.title: Pressure-Cooker Chicken and Chickpea Tagine
recipes.summary: Chicken thighs, chickpeas and dried apricots in a warm spiced sauce, ready in about 35 minutes in the pressure cooker.
steps: Use the sauté setting to soften the onion in the oil for 4 minutes, add the garlic and spices for 1 minute.
Add the chicken, chickpeas, tomatoes, apricots and stock, seal and cook at high pressure for 10 minutes, then release the pressure.
Check the chicken is cooked through at 75°C. Prepare the couscous with boiling water until the grains are tender, then serve the tagine over it with the coriander.
notes: Contains gluten (couscous).
Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C at the thickest part with no pink; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.

recipes.title: Sheet-Pan Garlic and Thyme Chicken with Potatoes and Green Beans
recipes.summary: Chicken thighs roasted on one tray with baby potatoes, lemon and thyme, with green beans added at the end.
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C. Toss the potatoes, garlic, lemon, thyme, oil and salt on a large tray, then nestle the chicken on top, skin side up.
Roast for 25 minutes, add the beans, and roast for 12 minutes more until the chicken is golden and cooked through.
Rest for 5 minutes and spoon the tray juices over to serve.
notes: Gluten free.
Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C at the thickest part with no pink; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.

recipes.title: Freezer-Batch Turkey and Vegetable Meatballs in Tomato Sauce
recipes.summary: Turkey meatballs with grated zucchini and carrot, simmered in tomato sauce and portioned for the freezer.
steps: Mix the mince, zucchini, carrot, crumbs, egg, parmesan and oregano and roll into 32 balls.
Soften the onion and garlic in the oil for 5 minutes, add the tomatoes and 1/2 cup of water, and bring to a simmer.
Add the meatballs, cover and simmer for 20 minutes, turning once, until cooked through.
Cool, portion into containers and freeze.
notes: Contains egg, dairy and gluten. Parmesan is not vegetarian.

Food safety: mince must reach 75°C throughout with no pink; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days. Freeze in portions for up to 3 months and thaw in the fridge overnight; reheat until steaming hot.

recipes.title: Slow-Cooker Pulled Pork Rolls with Apple Slaw
recipes.summary: Smoky pulled pork shoulder piled into rolls with a crisp apple and cabbage slaw.
steps: Rub the pork with the sugar, paprika, cumin and 1 teaspoon of salt, then set on the sliced onion in the slow cooker with the vinegar and stock.
Cook on low for 8 hours until the pork shreds easily, then shred and toss in the juices.
Toss the cabbage, apple and mayonnaise for the slaw and pile into the rolls with the pork.
notes: Contains egg, gluten and soy.
Food safety: pork must reach 70°C or more with no pink; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.

recipes.title: Pressure-Cooker Lamb and Chickpea Curry
recipes.summary: Tender lamb shoulder and chickpeas in a mild tomato curry sauce, pressure cooked in under an hour.
steps: Brown the lamb in the oil using the sauté setting for 6 minutes, then add the onion, garlic, ginger and spices for 3 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, chickpeas and stock, seal and cook at high pressure for 25 minutes, then release naturally.
Cook the rice separately until tender. Check the lamb is tender and steaming hot, then stir the yoghurt through the curry off the heat and serve.
notes: Contains dairy.
Food safety: cook lamb until tender and at least 75°C throughout; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.

recipes.title: One-Pot Lemon Chicken and Rice with Peas
recipes.summary: Chicken thighs and rice cooked together in one pot with lemon, garlic and peas.
steps: Brown the chicken in the oil in a lidded pot for 5 minutes, add the onion and garlic and cook for 3 minutes.
Stir in the rice, stock and lemon zest, cover and simmer on low for 18 minutes until the rice is tender.
Stir through the peas and lemon juice, rest covered for 5 minutes, then scatter with parsley.
notes: Gluten free.
Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C at the thickest part with no pink; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.

recipes.title: Sheet-Pan Baked Salmon with Broccolini and Sweet Potato
recipes.summary: Salmon fillets roasted with sweet potato wedges and broccolini on one tray, finished with lemon.
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C. Toss the sweet potato with half the oil, paprika and salt on a tray and roast for 15 minutes.
Add the broccolini and salmon, drizzle with the remaining oil, and roast for 12 minutes until the salmon flakes.
Serve with the lemon wedges.
notes: Gluten free and dairy free.
Food safety: cook fish until opaque and flaking, and shellfish until opaque and firm; keep raw seafood below 5°C, refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 1 day.

recipes.title: Freezer-Friendly Beef and Bean Burrito Parcels
recipes.summary: Beef mince, black beans and cheese rolled in tortillas, wrapped individually and frozen for quick lunches.
steps: Brown the mince and onion in the oil for 8 minutes, add the spices, tomato paste, beans and 1/2 cup of water and simmer for 8 minutes.
Cool the filling, then roll with the cheese into the tortillas and wrap each in baking paper.
Freeze, then reheat from frozen in a 180°C oven for 25 minutes or until steaming hot throughout.
notes: Contains dairy and gluten.

Food safety: mince must reach 75°C throughout with no pink; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days. Freeze in portions for up to 3 months and thaw in the fridge overnight; reheat until steaming hot.

recipes.title: Slow-Cooker Chicken Cacciatore with Olives
recipes.summary: Chicken thighs braised with capsicum, tomato and olives, served over soft polenta.
steps: Brown the chicken in the oil for 5 minutes and place in the slow cooker with the onion, capsicum, garlic, tomatoes, olives, stock and oregano.
Cook on low for 6 hours until the chicken falls from the bone.
Cook the polenta in 4 cups of water until thick, and serve under the chicken.
notes: Gluten free.
Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C at the thickest part with no pink; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.

recipes.title: High-Protein Chicken Burrito Bowl Meal Prep
recipes.summary: Four lunch boxes of spiced chicken, rice, black beans and corn with a lime yoghurt dressing.
steps: Cook the rice until tender and cool. Toss the chicken with the cumin, paprika and oil and pan-fry for 8 minutes until cooked through.
Divide the rice, chicken, beans, corn, tomato and lettuce into four containers.
Mix the yoghurt and lime and add a spoonful to each. Keep refrigerated.
notes: Contains dairy.
Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C at the thickest part with no pink; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days. Eat within 2 days of cooking when packed.

recipes.title: Pressure-Cooker Beef Ragu with Pappardelle
recipes.summary: A rich shredded beef and tomato ragu cooked fast in the pressure cooker and tossed through ribbon pasta.
steps: Brown the beef in the oil on the sauté setting, then add the onion, carrot, celery, garlic and tomato paste for 4 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, stock and rosemary, seal and cook at high pressure for 45 minutes, then release naturally.
Shred the beef into the sauce. Cook the pasta until tender, toss with the ragu and top with parmesan.
notes: Contains gluten, dairy and egg.
Food safety: cook beef until tender and steaming hot throughout (at least 75°C); refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 3 days.

recipes.title: Sheet-Pan Sausage and Vegetable Bake with Zucchini
recipes.summary: Pork sausages roasted with zucchini, red onion, capsicum and potatoes on one tray.
steps: Heat the oven to 210°C. Toss the potatoes, zucchini, onion, capsicum, oil, oregano and salt on a large tray.
Roast for 15 minutes, add the sausages and roast for 25 minutes more, turning once, until golden.
Check a sausage reaches 75°C in the centre with no pink, rest for 5 minutes and serve.
notes: Check the sausage label for gluten.
Food safety: pork must reach 70°C or more with no pink; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days. Sausages must reach 75°C.

recipes.title: Slow-Cooker Lentil and Sweet Potato Dal
recipes.summary: Red lentils and sweet potato simmered slowly with ginger and turmeric in coconut milk.
steps: Add the lentils, sweet potato, onion, garlic, ginger, spices, coconut milk and stock to the slow cooker.
Cook on low for 5 hours until the lentils are soft and the sweet potato is tender.
Stir in the spinach until wilted, about 2 minutes.
Cook the rice separately until tender and serve the dal over it.
notes: Vegan and gluten free.

recipes.title: Freezer-Batch Chicken and Vegetable Pot Pie Filling
recipes.summary: A creamy chicken, leek and pea filling frozen in portions, then topped with puff pastry and baked when needed.
steps: Melt the butter, soften the leek and carrot for 6 minutes, add the chicken and cook for 6 minutes.
Stir in the flour, then gradually add the milk and stock, and simmer for 10 minutes until thick. Add the peas and thyme, and cool.
Freeze the filling in 8 pots. To serve, thaw, top each with a pastry round and bake at 200°C for 25 minutes until golden and steaming hot.
notes: Contains dairy and gluten.

Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C at the thickest part with no pink; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days. Freeze in portions for up to 3 months and thaw in the fridge overnight; reheat until steaming hot.

recipes.title: Chicken and Rice Stir-Fry with Capsicum, Carrot and Spring Onion Greens
recipes.summary: A simple stir-fry that uses garlic-infused oil and the green tops of spring onion in place of garlic and onion.

items: 1 cup spring onion, green tops only, sliced

steps: Heat half the oil in a wok and stir-fry the chicken for 5 minutes until cooked through, then remove.
Add the remaining oil, capsicum, carrot and ginger and stir-fry for 4 minutes.
Return the chicken with the soy, vinegar, rice and spring onion greens and toss for 2 minutes until hot.
notes: Made with ingredient choices that avoid onion and garlic pieces; check the soy sauce label. Dairy free.
Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C at the thickest part with no pink; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.

recipes.title: Baked Salmon with Herbed Potatoes and Wilted Spinach
recipes.summary: Salmon with chive-and-parsley potatoes and spinach, using ingredients commonly chosen for low-FODMAP eating.
steps: Heat the oven to 210°C. Roast the potatoes with half the oil for 20 minutes.
Add the salmon, brush with oil, and roast for 10 minutes until it flakes.
Wilt the spinach in a hot pan for 1 minute, toss with the potatoes, herbs and lemon and serve with the salmon.
notes: Gluten free and dairy free.
Food safety: cook fish until opaque and flaking, and shellfish until opaque and firm; keep raw seafood below 5°C, refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 1 day.

recipes.title: Ramadan Iftar Lamb and Chickpea Stew
recipes.summary: A warming Moroccan-style stew of lamb, chickpeas, lentils and tomato, good for breaking the fast.
steps: Brown the lamb in the oil for 5 minutes, add the onion and celery for 4 minutes and the spices for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, lentils, chickpeas and stock, cover and simmer for 60 minutes until the lamb and lentils are tender.
Finish with the lemon and coriander and serve with the apricots on the side.
notes: Gluten free and dairy free.
Food safety: cook lamb until tender and at least 75°C throughout; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.

recipes.title: Suhoor Spiced Egg and Bean Shakshuka
recipes.summary: Eggs poached in a spiced tomato and white bean sauce, a filling pre-dawn meal served with wholemeal bread.
steps: Soften the onion and capsicum in the oil for 6 minutes, add the garlic and spices for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and beans, simmer for 8 minutes, then make 8 wells and crack in the eggs.
Cover and cook for 5 minutes until the whites are set and the yolks are firm enough. Serve with the bread.
notes: Contains egg and gluten.
Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites and yolks are set; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 1 day.

recipes.title: Shabbat Slow-Roast Chicken with Root Vegetables and Honey
recipes.summary: A whole chicken roasted over carrot, potato and onion with honey and thyme for a Friday night table.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C. Spread the vegetables in a deep tray, drizzle with half the oil and season.
Rub the chicken with the remaining oil, place the lemon inside, set on the vegetables and roast for 80 minutes, brushing with the honey in the last 20 minutes.
Check the thickest part of the thigh reaches 75°C, rest for 15 minutes, carve and serve with the tray juices.
notes: Gluten free and dairy free.
Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C at the thickest part with no pink; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.

recipes.title: Lunar New Year Braised Pork Belly with Star Anise and Eggs
recipes.summary: Slow-braised pork belly and boiled eggs in a sweet soy sauce, served with steamed rice.
steps: Boil the eggs for 8 minutes, cool and peel. Blanch the pork in boiling water for 5 minutes and drain.
Simmer the pork with the soy, sugar, star anise, ginger, garlic and water, covered, for 75 minutes until tender, adding the eggs for the last 15 minutes.
Steam the bok choy for 3 minutes until tender and serve everything over the rice.
notes: Contains egg, soy and gluten.
Food safety: pork must reach 70°C or more with no pink; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.

recipes.title: Lemon and Herb Pan-Seared Snapper with Roast Pumpkin
recipes.summary: Snapper fillets seared crisp-skinned with lemon zest, served on roast pumpkin with rocket.
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C and roast the pumpkin with half the oil for 25 minutes until golden.
Rub the fish with lemon zest, salt and the remaining oil and sear in a hot pan skin side down for 4 minutes, then turn for 2 minutes until opaque and flaking.
Serve on the pumpkin and rocket with the balsamic.
notes: Gluten free and dairy free.
Food safety: cook fish until opaque and flaking, and shellfish until opaque and firm; keep raw seafood below 5°C, refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 1 day.

recipes.title: Lemon and Herb-Crusted Lamb Rack with Roast Vegetables
recipes.summary: Lamb racks coated with lemon zest, thyme and breadcrumbs, roasted with carrot and potato.
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C. Roast the potato and carrot with 2 tablespoons of oil for 15 minutes.
Sear the lamb in the remaining oil for 3 minutes until browned, brush with mustard and press on the lemon zest, thyme and crumbs.
Add to the tray and roast for 15 to 18 minutes, then rest for 10 minutes before cutting into cutlets.
notes: Contains gluten.
Food safety: cook lamb racks to at least 63°C for medium, then rest for 3 minutes; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.
